identities.name: Ana Gonzalves
identities.note: Andres Gonzalves's crew on Fireball 14244, 2022-2024, all KSC. Her surname tracks his spelling row for row. Whether she is also the 'Ana Maria Grande' who crews the same boat is a question for the club, not a merge — see CLARIFICATIONS.md §9.

identities.name: Ana Maria Grande
identities.note: Five spellings of Andres Gonzalves's Fireball crew, 2019-2023, all KSC, never two in one series. The corpus splits 7/5/1/1/1 in favour of 'Ana-Marie Grande'; the Spanish form is published here to match his own name, and the correct spelling is unconfirmed.

identities.name: Andres Gonzalves
identities.note: One Fireball sailor, published under six spellings across 2019-2024 (all KSC, all Fireball). Confirmed by the club. The display name is the commonest; the correct spelling is still to be confirmed. The bare 'Andreas' is the 2020 Summer Series entry on Fireball 1471 with 'Ana' crewing — 1471 is this boat in every other year it appears.

identities.note: Fireball crew at the 2022 Munsters (DMYC) and the 2023 Munsters/Leinsters (Malahide YC). The clubs differ, which normally holds a pair apart — allowed here because the surname is rare enough that a one-letter variant is not a coincidence, both are Dublin clubs, and a sailor changing club between seasons is ordinary. Worth confirming.

identities.name: Leon Mullally

identities.name: Margaret Hynes
identities.note: Wayfarer 10826 with Mike Hayes crewing, in 2019 (Cullaun) and 2025 (KSC / Cullaun SC) — the same private boat and the same crew either side of a gap. 'Margaret Hayes' appears once, on the row where the crew cell immediately below reads 'Mike Hayes'; 'Margaret Hynes' appears twice, on rows where the two surnames differ. The doubled surname is read as the slip, so Hynes is published. CLARIFICATIONS.md §9 previously listed this pair as almost certainly two people; the crew field is what settled it.

identities.name: Tim O'Neill
identities.note: CLARIFICATIONS.md §9 previously held 'Timothy O'Neill' apart because it carried Cullaun rather than KSC. Reading crew as well as helms settled it: both spellings helm RS 200 1059 with Martin Bon in 2022 and with Aoibhí Ryan in 2023, and 'Tim O'Neill' himself is entered as Cullaun in 2022 and as 'Cullaun / KSC' in 2023.
